description: 1901 row 18-8: dark brown brick, 3 axes x 3 upper storeys, segmental-arched windows with stone keystone blocks, centre console balcony stack, brick corbel-table cornice; crowns: none, a square brick tower-dormer over the centre axis, or a stepped gable over the centre axis; every ground floor its own shop

tower.note: square brick tower-dormer with a two-light window rising one storey over the centre axis (16-18 middle and right, 14); top at strip row ~169-177 = 1.5-1.8 m over the parapet line -> rise 0.55 (3DBAG roof max 16.1 m; rise 1 overshot it by 1.6 m, height gate)

arched-tower.note: 12: the tower ends in a round arch over an arched light (modelled flat-topped); top at strip row ~164 = 2.0 m over the parapet -> rise 0.65

step-gable.note: 8-10: a stepped gable with one two-light attic window over the centre axis of each module; gable top at strip row 152, 2.1 m over the parapet line (row 235) -> crownRise 0.75; photo reader: trapgevel, 3 steps/side, span ~0.2-0.71 -> crownSteps 3

rhythm.identicalBays: upper storeys: 3 axes, centre axis a French window with a console balcony
rhythm.symmetry: each module symmetric about its centre axis (balconies, tower/gable)
rhythm.roofline: brick corbel-table cornice; tower-dormer or stepped gable over the centre axis
schemaLimits: the corbel table is modelled as a bracketed cornice
stone blocks in the window arches are approximated by keystones and stone arch rings
the tower-dormer windows are not drawn (a tower rising < 1 storey gets no light); the photo has one two-light window per tower

evidence.citation: strip.jpg pands 2-5 (2021-03-24): seven identical 3-axis modules (16-18 = 3, 8-10 = 2); detect-house-types.ts linked all seven at NCC >= 0.6
